title: M3 expanded local UI and application-service boundary decisions
goal: Record accepted D15-D19 decisions for UI topology, typed operations, protection status, CI activation separation and multi-project phasing.
acceptanceCriteria: V4-AD-040 expands the existing local Web Companion without creating a second policy engine, backend product or remote control plane.
Every future UI operation is classified and constrained by typed service, session, origin, CSRF, size, stale-confirmation, cancellation and receipt rules.
Protected status requires non-vacuous installed authority and enforced CI rather than a local or no-op pass.
CI candidate generation remains separate from Target mutation, pull-request work, trust authorization and remote activation.
V4-TODO-006 records read-only-first multi-project phasing and V4-TODO-021 tracks expanded UI implementation.
No product code, route, contract, test, workflow, ruleset, package, consumer repository or remote state changes occur.
risks: Expanding the UI could accidentally create a second execution or policy authority.
A generic browser-to-command gateway could bypass typed root and capability validation.
Setup convenience could collapse Target trust changes or remote activation into an implicit action.
Aggregate status could be expanded into unsafe parallel execution before isolation and resource ceilings exist.
decisions: D15 accepts expansion of the existing local Web Companion instead of a second Setup application.
D16 accepts typed operation classes and explicit local-web security controls.
D17 accepts a non-vacuous definition of protected that includes required repository enforcement.
D18 accepts local CI candidate generation while preserving Target and remote activation boundaries.
D19 accepts read-only multi-project aggregation before any bounded parallel execution.
